findings.title: Booking conversion is credited to the newest open lead regardless of service, so the wrong rep is credited and the lead that actually converted stays open
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p12.mjs — sets up an active assignment policy + SLA policy for team 'sales' covering grooming+boarding in Bengaluru, two active reps, then for one customer CU-1 creates two open leads: LEAD-BOARD (service 'boarding', assigned_at now-24h) and LEAD-GROOM (service 'grooming', assigned_at now-1h). assignLead gives LEAD-BOARD to neha@pawspace.in and LEAD-GROOM to rahul@pawspace.in. It then inserts canonical_bookings BK-1 (customer CU-1, service_code 'boarding') with booking_payments PAY-1 status 'captured' and calls attributeBookingToOpenLead(db,{customerId:'CU-1',bookingId:'BK-1'}), then generateSalesProductivityFacts over the enclosing period.
findings.measured_before:
LEAD-BOARD owner: neha@pawspace.in | LEAD-GROOM owner: rahul@pawspace.in
attributeBookingToOpenLead(BK-1 = boarding) -> {"leadId":"LEAD-GROOM","converted":true}
leads: [{"id":"LEAD-BOARD","service":"boarding","owner":"neha@pawspace.in","status":"active","converted_booking_id":null},{"id":"LEAD-GROOM","service":"grooming","owner":"rahul@pawspace.in","status":"converted","converted_booking_id":"BK-1"}]
bookingConversions per rep: [{"email":"neha@pawspace.in","conversions":0},{"email":"rahul@pawspace.in","conversions":1}]

Also reproduced in /tmp/lg/p7.mjs for the second hop: convertLeadOnPaymentCaptured(db,{customerId:'CU-1',bookingId:'BK-2'}) where BK-2 has service_code 'food' and was never attributed to any lead returned {"leadId":"LEAD-BOARD"} and set LEAD-BOARD status='converted', converted_booking_id='BK-2'.
findings.expected: A booking should only convert a lead whose service matches the booking's service_code (or, failing a match, convert nothing and leave the leads open for a human to attribute). The lead that was actually worked for that service must be the one credited, and a lead for a different service must stay open.
findings.consequence: Rahul is shown 1 booking conversion he did not produce and Neha is shown 0 for the boarding booking she actually closed — sales-productivity-governance.ts joins canonical_bookings to lead_work_items.converted_booking_id to lead_assignments, so the credit follows the mis-attributed lead into every per-rep productivity fact and into the revenue-mission command centre's owner breakdown. Separately, Neha's real boarding lead is left status='active', so the customer who already booked and paid keeps getting called by Sales; and Rahul's live grooming lead is closed as 'converted' so the grooming opportunity is never worked.
findings.rule_source: lib/lead-conversion-attribution.ts own comment above ensureLeadWorkItemsTable: "initiated_booking_id records WHICH booking a lead was linked to before payment, so the later payment-capture conversion credits that exact lead. Without it, a customer with two open leads could have the wrong one marked converted (attribution went to whichever was newest)." The module states the rule but only applied it to the payment-capture hop; the selection query in attributeBookingToOpenLead is still ORDER BY assigned_at DESC LIMIT 1 with no service predicate, and convertLeadOnPaymentCaptured still falls back to it. What should happen when no lead matches the service is NONE -> decision ledger: is a service-mismatched conversion an error, a no-op, or a manual-attribution queue item?
findings.suggested_fix: Add the booking's service_code to the lead selection in attributeBookingToOpenLead (match lead_work_items.service, normalised the same way lead-assignment-governance.ts leadContext does) and return null rather than converting an unrelated lead when nothing matches. In convertLeadOnPaymentCaptured, drop the ORDER BY ... ELSE 1 fallback entirely: if no lead carries initiated_booking_id = this booking, credit nothing.

findings.title: A breached SLA clock is flipped to 'met' by a late action, so the same first-response clock is counted as both met and breached in the productivity report
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p3.mjs — 10-minute first_response SLA policy (elapsed business hours), lead assigned to neha@pawspace.in, startLeadSlaClock at t0. runLeadSlaGovernance at t0+15min breaches it. recordLeadSlaAction at t0+25min (15 minutes past the deadline) with outcome 'connected_interested'. Then saveSalesProductivityPolicy + activateSalesProductivityPolicy + generateSalesProductivityFacts over the period.
findings.expected: A clock whose action landed after due_at must not read 'met'. Either it stays 'breached' with the late action recorded, or it moves to a distinct terminal state such as 'met_late'. Whatever the state, met + breached must never exceed the number of clocks.
findings.consequence: For one first-response clock the productivity fact reports firstResponseClocks=1, firstResponseMet=1 AND firstResponseBreached=1 — a 200% denominator, so any compliance percentage a manager computes from that row is wrong in both directions. At the same time revenue-mission-command-center.ts counts breaches as status='breached' and therefore reports slaBreached=0 for the same clock, so the two management surfaces flatly contradict each other. leadSlaDirectory shows display.state 'met' with no indication the deadline was missed, and lead_work_items.status is reset from 'sla_breached' back to 'active', erasing the breach from the lead worklist too.
findings.rule_source: lib/sales-productivity-governance.ts generateSalesProductivityFacts counts met as `SUM(CASE WHEN c.status='met' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` and breached as `SUM(CASE WHEN c.breached_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` over the same `COUNT(*) total` — the module's own contract is that met and breached partition the clocks. lib/lead-sla-governance.ts runLeadSlaGovernance writes breached_at with COALESCE, i.e. treats the breach as a durable fact. Whether a late action should be allowed to clear a breach at all is NONE -> decision ledger: does PawSpace want 'met_late' as a distinct state, or does a breach stay breached forever?
findings.suggested_fix: In recordLeadSlaAction, set status='met' only when now <= clock.due_at; otherwise set a distinct state (e.g. 'met_late') and leave breached_at intact, and do not reset lead_work_items.status from 'sla_breached'. Make the productivity met counter mutually exclusive with the breach counter (`c.status='met' AND c.breached_at IS NULL`) so the two can never both fire on one row.

findings.title: Idempotency keys in the lead engine do not bind the mutation context: reusing a key on a different lead silently no-ops and returns another lead's record as success
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p4.mjs — creates LEAD-A and LEAD-B under an active assignment policy and SLA policy, then calls each of the three functions twice with the SAME idempotencyKey but a DIFFERENT leadId (and, for the clock, a different clockType).
findings.expected: A replay guard must reject a key that was already consumed for a different lead / clock type / outcome, the way the rest of this repo does — with a 409-shaped error, not a success-shaped duplicatePrevented object describing a different entity.
findings.consequence: All three POST actions take idempotencyKey verbatim from the request body (app/api/lead-assignment-governance/route.ts action 'assign'/'reassign', app/api/lead-sla-governance/route.ts action 'start_clock'/'record_action'). A UI or retry wrapper that reuses a key across leads — a per-session key, a per-user key, a copy-pasted curl — makes the second lead silently vanish from the pipeline: LEAD-B is never assigned (owner stays 'Unassigned'), never gets an SLA clock, and a rep's genuine logged call on LEAD-B is discarded while the API returns 200 with lead A's event. The rep sees success, the manager sees an untouched lead breaching SLA, and the audit row written by securityAudit records duplicatePrevented against the wrong lead.
findings.rule_source: In-repo convention, two independent precedents: lib/customer-account.ts mutateCustomerAccount — `if(String(prior.customer_id)!==customerId||String(prior.action)!==action) throw new Response("Idempotency key was already used for a different customer mutation",{status:409})`; and lib/referral-governance.ts claimReferral / reserveReferralReward — "Referral idempotency key was already used for different claim context" / "Referral reward idempotency key was already used for a different reservation". The lead engine is the outlier.
findings.suggested_fix: After the prior-row lookup in assignLead, startLeadSlaClock and recordLeadSlaAction, compare the stored context to the request (lead_id; lead_id+clock_type for the clock; lead_id+outcome for the action) and throw a 409-shaped 'idempotency key was already used for a different ...' instead of returning the other entity as duplicatePrevented.

findings.title: SLA auto-reassignment parks a breached lead on employee_email NULL in a fallback queue nothing reads, reports autoReassigned:1, and on the next cycle hands it straight back to the agent that failed it
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p10.mjs — same policy setup as p3 but only ONE eligible member for the service/city (rahul@pawspace.in deactivated). LEAD-A assigned to neha@pawspace.in, first_response clock started at t0 (due +10m, manager +30m, reassignment +60m). runLeadSlaGovernance at t0+70min, then again at t0+140min. Also `grep -rn "fallback_queue" lib app` outside lead-assignment-governance.ts returns zero matches — nothing in the codebase ever reads the column.
findings.expected: When no eligible agent other than the failing one exists, the sweep must not report autoReassigned:1. It should either leave the assignment with the current agent and raise the manager escalation it already has an event type for (auto_reassignment_failed / escalateToManager:true), or route to a fallback queue that some surface actually reads. It must never re-hand the lead to the exact agent the reassignment was meant to take it away from.
findings.consequence: For one full sweep cycle the SLA-breached lead has no owner at all: lead_work_items.owner='Unassigned', lead_assignments.employee_email=NULL. Every owner-scoped surface drops it — staff-alert-center.ts keys its lead_sla_breach alerts off a.employee_email, dueLeadCallbacks filters on l.owner, outboundBatchStatus filters on a.employee_email — and leadAssignmentIntegrity reports 0 mismatches because it COALESCEs NULL and 'Unassigned' to the same value, so the integrity check that exists to catch exactly this says everything is fine. fallback_queue='queue-blr' is written and read by nothing anywhere in lib/ or app/. Meanwhile the sweep's own return value says autoReassigned:1 and an auto_reassigned event is emitted with newAgent:null — a success-shaped signal for work that did not happen. On the next cycle reassignLead computes excludeEmployeeEmail as `input.excludeEmployeeEmail ?? text(current.employee_email)`, and text(null) is the empty string, which candidateRows treats as falsy and ignores — so the exclusion is silently dropped and the lead goes back to neha@pawspace.in, the agent who breached it. The lead then ping-pongs between 'nobody' and 'the failing agent' forever, breaching on every cycle.
findings.rule_source: lib/lead-sla-governance.ts writes its own reassignment reason as "Automatic SLA reassignment - reassignment threshold passed for the previous agent (…)" and already carries an auto_reassignment_failed event with escalateToManager:true, so the module's stated intent is that the lead moves AWAY from the failing agent or a manager is told. What should happen when the team has no second eligible agent is NONE -> decision ledger: hold with the current agent + manager alert, or a fallback queue with a real worklist behind it?
findings.suggested_fix: In runLeadSlaGovernance, treat a reassignment that returns employee_email == null as a failure: do not increment autoReassigned, do not cancel the clock, emit auto_reassignment_failed with escalateToManager:true. In reassignLead, use `input.excludeEmployeeEmail ?? (text(current.employee_email) || null)` so an unassigned predecessor does not silently clear the exclusion, and make leadAssignmentIntegrity flag employee_email IS NULL as its own class rather than COALESCEing it to 'Unassigned'.

findings.title: Any customer can rebind another customer's app install to themselves through the public OTP verify endpoint, erasing the victim from acquisition attribution and from the App-Inbound lead sweep
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p13.mjs — drives the real public path end to end, no direct DB writes for the hijack. recordAppInstall('DEVICE-ALICE-01', source 'google_ads', campaign 'diwali'). Alice: requestCustomerOtp('9990001111') -> verifyCustomerOtp({challengeId, code, name:'Alice', installId:'DEVICE-ALICE-01'}). Bob: requestCustomerOtp('8880002222') -> verifyCustomerOtp({challengeId, code, name:'Bob', installId:'DEVICE-ALICE-01'}) — Bob simply puts Alice's install id in his own request body. Then acquisitionFunnelReport and runAppFunnelSweep. app/api/customer-otp/route.ts:17 POST has no authorize() call and passes body.installId straight through; lib/customer-otp.ts:72 calls identifyInstall with it.
findings.measured_before:
Alice customerId: CUS-OTP-2A94964BFDF3C7D6765E46BA
link after Alice: [{"install_id":"DEVICE-ALICE-01","customer_id":"CUS-OTP-2A94964BFDF3C7D6765E46BA","identified_at":1787564992260}]
Bob customerId: CUS-OTP-E35736DD1EBAA837E2977FAE
link after Bob: [{"install_id":"DEVICE-ALICE-01","customer_id":"CUS-OTP-E35736DD1EBAA837E2977FAE","identified_at":1787564992260}]
acquisitionFunnelReport: {"appAcquisitionFunnel":{"downloads":1,"identified":1,"anonymous":0,"converted":0,"paymentPending":0,"noBooking":1,...}}
sweep: {...,"appInboundLeads":1,...}
leads created for: [{"id":"LWI-192B0665-B3F","customer_id":"CUS-OTP-E35736DD1EBAA837E2977FAE","source":"App Inbound","owner":"Rahul"}]
(The only App-Inbound lead created belongs to Bob. Alice — an identified app user with no booking — got none.)
findings.expected: An install already bound to a different customer must not be silently re-bound by a second customer's request. Either the first binding wins and the second is ignored/flagged, or the rebinding is recorded as a distinct device-transfer event for review. The ON CONFLICT clause currently makes last-writer-wins with no check and no audit.
findings.consequence: Bob steals the paid-acquisition attribution of Alice's Google Ads install: install_identity_links now says DEVICE-ALICE-01 belongs to Bob, and identified_at still carries Alice's timestamp. Alice disappears from the identified cohort entirely (downloads=1, identified=1, and the single identity row is Bob's), so acquisitionFunnelReport's conversionRateFromIdentified and conversionRateFromDownloads are computed on a corrupted denominator. Concretely, the funnel sweep's rule 'identified app user with NO booking -> App-Inbound Sales lead' fires for Bob and never for Alice — a real prospective customer is permanently dropped from the sales pipeline by another user's request body. The install id is a client-side device identifier sent to an unauthenticated endpoint, so it is guessable/observable, and the whole call is wrapped in .catch(()=>{}) so nothing is logged when it happens.
findings.rule_source: In-repo convention that a body-supplied id must be ownership-checked before it is written: lib/customer-account.ts mutateCustomerAccount — `if(owned&&String(owned.customer_id)!==customerId)throw new Response("Address ownership denied",{status:403})`; lib/referral-governance.ts ensureReferralCode — "Referrer must be a canonical customer". identifyInstall does neither. Whether a legitimate device handover (shared phone, resold handset) should be permitted, and by what evidence, is NONE -> decision ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the binding first-write-wins: change the upsert in identifyInstall to `ON CONFLICT(install_id) DO NOTHING` (or `DO UPDATE ... WHERE install_identity_links.customer_id = excluded.customer_id`) and, when the existing customer_id differs, write an install_identity_conflicts row for review instead of overwriting. Also validate customerId against canonical_customers before inserting.

findings.title: scheduleLeadCallback has no upper bound on requestedAt, so a far-future time supersedes the real callback promise and removes the lead from both the callback queue and the missed-callback sweep permanently
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p9.mjs — LEAD-1 gets a genuine callback for now+30min. Then scheduleLeadCallback is called again for the same lead with requestedAt = now + 100*365*86400000 (year 2126), the shape lib/haptik-integration-governance.ts captureHaptikCallback produces when an external bot supplies preferredAt (its only guard is `Number.isFinite(preferred) && preferred > now`). Then dueLeadCallbacks with a 120-minute look-ahead and runLeadCallbackSweep one day later.
findings.expected: requestedAt must be bounded on both sides. The function already refuses a past time as 'not a placeholder'; a time decades out is equally a placeholder and should be rejected (or clamped) rather than accepted and allowed to supersede a real promise.
findings.consequence: The genuine promise made to the customer ('call me at 4pm today') is marked superseded and the lead's next_action_at is pushed to 2126. dueLeadCallbacks filters on requested_at <= lookAhead so the callback never appears in any rep or manager feed again, and runLeadCallbackSweep only marks 'missed' when requested_at <= asOf - 15min, so it is never flagged missed either — {processed:0, missed:0}. The lead silently leaves every worklist with no alert. The reachable trigger is captureHaptikCallback passing an external bot's preferredAt through unchecked: a units error (seconds vs ms), a timezone/epoch bug, or a hostile payload all land here, and lib/bot-call-disposition.ts feeds callbackAt in the same way.
findings.rule_source: lib/lead-callback-governance.ts scheduleLeadCallback's own guard — `if(!Number.isFinite(input.requestedAt)||input.requestedAt<=Date.now())throw new Error("Callback time must be a real, future time - not a placeholder")` — establishes that placeholder times must be refused; only the lower half of the bound was implemented. What the maximum callback horizon should be (7 days? 90 days?) is NONE -> decision ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit upper bound alongside the existing lower bound in scheduleLeadCallback and reject beyond it, e.g. `if(input.requestedAt > Date.now() + MAX_CALLBACK_HORIZON_MS) throw new Error(...)`, with the horizon a named constant next to missedGraceMinutes. Apply the same bound to preferredAt in captureHaptikCallback so the bot payload is rejected at the boundary rather than normalised into a valid-looking row.

findings.title: The public contact form performs no dedup: three identical submissions from one phone create three customers, three leads and three tasks owned by three different reps
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/lg/p6.mjs — calls the real route three times with an identical body {name:'Asha Rao', phone:'9876543210', email:'asha@example.com', area:'Bangalore', service:'Grooming', message:'need grooming'} and cf-connecting-ip 1.2.3.4, within the same second.
findings.expected: A submission whose normalised phone already exists as a recent crm_contact should attach to that contact (as a new activity, and at most refreshing the existing open lead) rather than minting a new customer id, a new lead and a new owner. If a duplicate is genuinely ambiguous it should be flagged for review, not silently multiplied.
findings.consequence: One person who double-clicks Submit, or resubmits after a slow response, becomes three customers in the CRM. Three different reps each get a 'First response to new website lead' task due in 10 minutes for the same human, so the customer is cold-called three times by three people — the exact experience failure the 10-minute SLA exists to prevent. Downstream every funnel denominator is inflated: three 'New lead' contacts and three lead_work_items for one real prospect, so conversion rate is understated by 3x for that prospect, and whichever rep happens to convert gets the credit while the other two carry permanently-dead leads. The three contacts also have three distinct customer ids, so customer-360 / lifetime-value views split one person's history three ways.
findings.rule_source: lib/revenue-opportunity-governance.ts already treats a possible-duplicate customer as a blocking condition — SuppressionReason includes 'duplicate_review_required' and createCanonicalRevenueOpportunity sets status 'review_required' when facts.issues includes 'possible_duplicate'. The repo's stated position is that duplicate customer identity must be reviewed, not silently accepted; this front door creates the duplicates that engine is meant to catch, and does so in crm_contacts, which that engine never reads. The exact dedup window and match rule (phone only? phone+name? 24h? forever?) is NONE -> decision ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the batch insert, look up crm_contacts by normalised phone. On a hit, insert only the crm_activity against the existing contact id and skip the new crm_contact / crm_task / lead_work_item when an open lead for that contact already exists; return the existing leadId. Where the match is uncertain, write the lead with a duplicate_review flag rather than assigning it to a second rep.

findings.title: The public relocation enquiry endpoint accepts impossible calendar dates, unbounded field lengths and unlimited anonymous submissions, while the sibling public lead endpoint enforces all three

An unauthenticated write endpoint must be rate-limited per origin the way the other public lead endpoint in this repo is.

In app/api/relocation-enquiry/route.ts POST, reuse the public_contact_rate_limits abuse gate before parsing the body.

findings.title: Pricing Control ignores a package's effective_from/effective_to, so a price scheduled for the future is charged today and a retired price is charged forever
findings.reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p5.mjs (route-level, no library shortcuts). It imports app/api/pricing-control/route.ts and app/api/boarding-commercial/route.ts, then:
1. POST /api/boarding-commercial {packageCode:'boarding-24h',petCount:2,scheduledStart:+7d,scheduledEnd:+7d+48h,paymentMode:'prepaid'} -> baseline quote.
2. PATCH /api/pricing-control {entity:'package',id:'canonical_boarding_24h',changes:{active:1,base_price:2500,effective_from:'2027-01-01'},reason:'ops scheduling a price change'} -- effective_from is in the PATCH allow-list at app/api/pricing-control/route.ts (`allowed` for entity 'package' includes 'effective_from','effective_to').
3. Repeat the same customer quote TODAY (system date 2026-08-24).
4. PATCH again to {base_price:150,effective_from:'2026-01-01',effective_to:'2026-01-31'} (a promo that ended 7 months ago) and quote again.
Also reproduced independently for grooming in /tmp/probe/p14.mjs against lib/grooming-governance.ts governGroomingBooking, and for the raw resolver in /tmp/probe/p3.mjs.
findings.expected: resolveLivePrice should only honour a service_packages row whose effective window contains the booking's scheduledStart, i.e. the same predicate every vertical already applies to its own catalogue (`activePackage` in lib/boarding-governance.ts:39, lib/sitting-governance.ts, lib/training-commercial-governance.ts) and the same predicate lib/pricing-engine.ts:11 `activeOn` already applies to dynamic_pricing_rules. A row dated 2027-01-01 must not price a 2026-08-31 stay; a row whose effective_to is 2026-01-31 must fall back to the vertical's catalogue price. Concretely, step 3 should still have returned total 2796 and step 5 should also have returned 2796.
findings.consequence: An operator using the Pricing Control panel exactly as designed - scheduling a price rise for the next quarter, or ending a January promotion by setting effective_to - changes the price customers are charged RIGHT NOW. In the reproduction an identical 2-night, 2-pet Luxury Stay went from Rs 2,796 to Rs 12,500 the instant a 2027-dated row was saved, and to Rs 752 when a long-dead January promo row was saved. The wrong figure is what the customer sees at checkout, what is written to boarding_commercial_quotes.total_amount, what governBoardingBooking then enforces on confirmation, and what lands in booking_payments.amount. The panel shows the operator the effective dates it just stored, so the operator has no way to see that they are not being honoured. This is the single lookup behind Boarding, Pet Sitting, Training and Grooming pricing (lib/live-commercial-quotes.ts, lib/training-commercial-governance.ts:29, lib/grooming-governance.ts:74, lib/live-grooming-governance.ts) and the public /api/live-price-quote the customer grooming flow renders from (app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx:91).
findings.rule_source: lib/pricing-engine.ts:11 `activeOn` (the same module already enforces the effective window for dynamic_pricing_rules); lib/boarding-governance.ts:39 / lib/sitting-governance.ts / lib/training-commercial-governance.ts `activePackage` (every vertical enforces effective_from/effective_to on its own catalogue); app/api/pricing-control/route.ts `allowed` list, which exposes effective_from/effective_to as operator-editable package fields.
findings.suggested_fix: In resolveLivePrice, filter the package row on the booking date the same way rules are filtered: `SELECT * FROM service_packages WHERE package_code=? AND active=1 AND effective_from<=? AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to>=?)` bound with input.scheduledStart.slice(0,10) twice, so a row outside its window falls through to `{price: input.fallbackPrice, source:'fallback_default'}`. app/api/pricing-quote/route.ts:ensureSchema/POST carries the identical unfiltered lookup and needs the same change.

findings.title: A Pet Sitting booking confirmed through /api/canonical-bookings is priced entirely by the client - any amount, any invented package code

Uses a REAL, non-preview actor: host app.pawspace.in (so isDevelopmentPreview is false), app_users row role_code='customer' (permissions ['pricing.view','scheduling.book'] per lib/platform-security.ts:24), customer_identity_links binding that email to CUS-P8, request header oai-authenticated-user-email: cust@example.com. lib/api-gateway.ts:125 maps POST /api/canonical-bookings to exactly 'scheduling.book', which this role holds.
Seed the scheduling graph (scheduling_assignment_decisions status='assigned' + one scheduling_reservations row with service_code='pet_sitting', matching city/zone/customer), then POST /api/canonical-bookings with serviceCode:'pet_sitting' and totalAmount set by the caller. findings.rule_source: app/api/sitting-bookings/route.ts + lib/sitting-governance.ts governSittingBooking ('Sitting amount does not match the server quote', 409) - the platform's own definition of a correctly priced Pet Sitting confirmation. The in-file comment at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:391 ('Pet Sitting on this path is client-priced (no server quote yet)') acknowledges the gap but the governed path now exists.

If /api/canonical-bookings is not meant to serve Pet Sitting at all now that /api/sitting-bookings exists, remove 'pet_sitting' from the `services` set at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:26 and return 409 pointing at the governed route.

findings.title: PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV unset or empty disables verify-first, so a client-declared "captured" payment is persisted as financial truth
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p12.mjs. Same real non-preview `customer` actor as the previous finding. The probe mutates only the workers env object between otherwise identical POSTs to /api/canonical-bookings, each carrying payment:{method:'upi',mode:'prepaid',status:'captured'}, and reads back booking_payments.status. Values tried: undefined (never bound), 'live', 'production', '' (empty string), 'SANDBOX_TYPO'.
findings.expected: The gate should fail CLOSED on absence: an unbound or blank PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV should select the STRICTER behaviour (liveMode = true, verify-first, client 'captured' demoted to 'created'), and only an explicit, recognised opt-in such as 'sandbox' should relax it. `String(env.PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV||"sandbox")` does the opposite: the single value that switches verify-first OFF is also the value you get for free when the binding is missing.
findings.consequence: A production Worker deployed without the PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV binding - or with it accidentally blanked - silently accepts the customer app's own claim that money was captured. booking_payments.status is written 'captured' with no gateway event, the booking_lifecycle_events 'payment_recorded' entry records status 'captured', and (per the same flag at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:193) entitlementActive becomes true so a Grooming subscription is created 'active' with its sessions reserved against a payment nobody verified. Every other spelling, including a typo, is safe; only the default-on-absence is unsafe, which is exactly the configuration state nobody tests. Note the code around it was clearly hardened for verify-first (the long comment at lines 30-46 and the offlineAuthorized permission check) - the polarity of this one flag undoes it when the binding is absent.
findings.rule_source: The route's own stated invariant at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:30-46: 'an ONLINE booking payment may NOT self-declare "captured"; it is recorded "created" and only a signature-verified Razorpay webhook may mark it captured' and 'It FAILS CLOSED on the method.' The environment flag that decides whether that rule applies at all does not fail closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert the default: `const raw=String(env.PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV??"").trim().toLowerCase(); const liveMode = raw !== "sandbox";` so an unset or blank binding yields liveMode=true. If a hard failure is preferable to a silent strict default, throw at request time when the binding is absent rather than inferring sandbox.

findings.title: Boarding catalogue GET keeps advertising the old per-pet price after Pricing Control is activated, while the quote POST on the same page charges the new one
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p11.mjs. Calls the real GET and POST handlers of app/api/boarding-commercial/route.ts against one database, before and after `UPDATE service_packages SET active=1,base_price=2500 WHERE package_code='boarding-24h'` (dynamic_pricing_rules emptied first so the number is unambiguous). GET drives the package picker in app/boarding/page.tsx, which renders `money(item.base_price_per_pet)` as '<price> / pet / unit'; POST drives the sticky quote panel on the same page.
findings.expected: Both halves of the same screen should read the same price source. GET /api/boarding-commercial -> listBoardingPackages reads boarding_commercial_packages.base_price_per_pet directly and never consults resolveLivePrice, while POST -> createLiveBoardingQuote does. After activation the picker should have shown 2500 / pet / unit, or the quote should have stayed at 699. The same split exists for Pet Sitting: app/sitting/page.tsx renders `activePackage.base_price_per_pet` from listSittingPackages while POST /api/sitting-commercial prices through createLiveSittingQuote.
findings.consequence: The customer picks 'Luxury Stay' from a card that says Rs 699 / pet / unit and the quote panel underneath it says Rs 5,000 for the same two nights and one pet. There is no third surface to arbitrate, and nothing on the page explains the difference, so the advertised price and the charged price disagree on a single screen for as long as any operator price is active in Pricing Control. This is the customer-visible face of the same bridge as the effective-window defect; it bites even when the operator's dates are entirely correct.
findings.rule_source: lib/live-pricing-resolver.ts is documented as the single bridge between the operator's Pricing Control state and customer price ('If the row remains inactive, callers get their pre-existing fallback unchanged'). The catalogue listing endpoint that feeds the same screen bypasses that bridge, so the two surfaces are not reading the same truth.
findings.suggested_fix: Route listBoardingPackages / listSittingPackages results through resolveLivePrice for the requested scheduledStart, city and zone before returning them from the GET handlers (one resolve per listed package), so the picker and the quote both come from the operator-controlled price. The GET already receives scheduledStart, cityId and zoneId.

findings.title: A confirmed Sitting/Boarding booking stores a price decomposition that does not add up to the amount charged
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p10.mjs. Activates the canonical Overnight Sitting price at 1200 in service_packages (dynamic_pricing_rules emptied), calls lib/live-commercial-quotes.ts createLiveSittingQuote for 1 pet over a 48h window, then calls lib/sitting-governance.ts governSittingBooking with the quote's own amounts. The returned object is exactly what app/api/sitting-bookings/route.ts:51 serialises into canonical_bookings.pricing_json (basePricePerPet, extraPetPrice, billableUnits). lib/boarding-governance.ts:51 governBoardingBooking has the identical shape - it returns basePricePerPet from the joined `p.base_price_per_pet`, not from the priced quote.
findings.expected: The unit price persisted alongside the total must be the unit price that produced the total. governSittingBooking selects `q.*,p.name,p.base_price_per_pet,p.extra_pet_price` and returns the PACKAGE columns, but createLiveSittingQuote already overwrote sitting_commercial_quotes.total_amount with the live-resolved price and never writes the live unit price back to the quote row - so the join can only ever return the stale catalogue figure. Either the quote row should carry the priced unit amounts, or the governed result should derive them from total_amount / billableUnits. Expected here: basePricePerPet 1200, 1200 x 2 = 2400.
findings.consequence: A booking that charged Rs 2,400 is recorded as 'Rs 799 per night x 2 nights'. Anyone reconciling the booking - a finance reviewer, an invoice line, a support agent explaining the charge to a customer disputing it, or any report that recomputes revenue from the unit breakdown - gets a figure Rs 802 short of what was actually taken, with no marker that the two disagree. It only shows up once an operator activates a live price, which is precisely when someone is most likely to be checking the numbers. The same applies to Boarding via governBoardingBooking, whose result is serialised into pricing_json.boardingCommercial by app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts.
findings.rule_source: Internal consistency of the record the route itself writes: app/api/sitting-bookings/route.ts:51 persists basePricePerPet, extraPetPrice and billableUnits next to total_amount as a decomposition of that total. No product decision is needed - the two fields are claims about the same transaction and they contradict each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist the priced unit amounts on the quote row. In lib/live-commercial-quotes.ts, extend the existing `UPDATE sitting_commercial_quotes SET total_amount=?,amount_due_now=?` (and the boarding equivalent) to also store base_price_per_pet / extra_pet_price columns on the quote, then have governSittingBooking / governBoardingBooking read those quote columns instead of joining the package table for price.

findings.title: Stay balance idempotency key is globally unique instead of per booking, so reusing one key across two bookings settles the second with no capture event recorded
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p9.mjs. Creates two split schedules (BK-A and BK-B, both pending_balance, balance 2000) via staySplitScheduleStatement, then calls payStayBalance twice with DIFFERENT bookingIds and the SAME idempotencyKey 'same-key-both', and dumps both tables. The key reaches this function straight from the request body: app/api/stay-balance/route.ts POST reads `body.idempotencyKey` and passes it through unmodified.
findings.expected: Two settlements should produce two 'balance_captured' rows in stay_payment_events. An idempotency key must bind the mutation it de-duplicates - here (bookingId, key) - so that the same key against a DIFFERENT booking is a different operation, not a replay. The gateway path in lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts:128 already namespaces its key as `gateway:${eventId}`, showing the key space is meant to be scoped; the customer path uses the caller's raw string with no scope at all.
findings.consequence: BK-B's balance is durably marked paid, with a payment_ref, and there is no capture event for it anywhere. The catch block that swallowed the insert is commented 'the same request already recorded its capture' - which is false: a different booking's capture is what occupied the key. stay_payment_events is the only per-capture trail this flow writes (the schedule row keeps just the latest ref), so a finance reconciliation or ops alert counting captures sees one where two occurred. Any client that derives its idempotency key from something other than the booking - a session id, a device id, a customer-scoped counter, a retry wrapper reusing one key for a batch - produces this silently, and the API returns 201 with duplicatePrevented:false both times so nothing warns the caller.
findings.rule_source: lib/stay-split-payments.ts:75 comment ('UNIQUE(idempotency_key) collision: the same request already recorded its capture') states the intended semantics; the schema's global UNIQUE on idempotency_key does not implement them. Cross-checked against lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts:128, which namespaces the same column.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the key to the booking at the point of use: bind `${bookingId}:${idempotencyKey}` (and correspondingly `gateway:${eventId}` stays distinct), or replace the single-column UNIQUE with UNIQUE(booking_id, idempotency_key). Either way, only swallow the UNIQUE error when a row for THIS booking_id already holds the key - otherwise the capture must be recorded.

findings.title: A NaN pet count passes the 1..max_pets guard in every stay/programme quote; only a NOT NULL column stops it, turning a bad input into a 500 on an unauthenticated endpoint
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p6.mjs sweeps petCount across 1, 0, -2, 4, 5, "abc", {}, [], null, true, 2.9 and 1e15 through the real POST handlers of app/api/boarding-commercial, app/api/sitting-commercial and app/api/training-commercial (all three mapped to no permission at lib/api-gateway.ts:14, i.e. reachable anonymously). The routes coerce with `Number(body.petCount||0)`, and the libs then apply `const petCount=Math.floor(Number(input.petCount)); if(petCount<1||petCount>Number(row.max_pets)) throw 409`. NaN<1 is false and NaN>4 is false, so NaN passes both comparisons.
findings.expected: A non-numeric pet count is a malformed request and belongs in the same 409/400 as 0 and 5 - `Boarding supports 1-4 pets per booking`. The guard should test membership, not two inequalities: `if(!Number.isInteger(petCount)||petCount<1||petCount>max)`. Instead the only thing standing between NaN and a persisted quote is the pet_count NOT NULL column; every arithmetic result downstream of it (totalAmount = basePricePerPet*petCount*stayUnits in Boarding, minutesPerSession = petCount*(direct+coaching) in Training at lib/training-commercial-governance.ts:29) is already NaN by the time the insert fails.
findings.consequence: Three anonymous, unauthenticated quote endpoints return HTTP 500 on an input that should be a clean 4xx, and each one logs a database constraint error. That is a bad-request-shaped payload producing a server-error-shaped response: it pollutes error budgets and alerting, and it hides the real problem from the caller. The containment is accidental rather than designed - the guard itself is NaN-blind, so any future column that is nullable, or any code path that uses petCount before the insert, inherits a NaN with no guard in front of it. Reachable with no credentials at all (lib/api-gateway.ts:14 maps these routes to no permission).
findings.rule_source: The routes' own stated bound, returned verbatim as `Boarding supports 1-4 pets per booking` / `Sitting supports 1-4 pets per booking` / `Training supports 1-4 pets per programme`. NaN satisfies neither side of that bound and is being treated as satisfying it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `petCount<1||petCount>max` with an explicit integer check in lib/boarding-governance.ts:47, lib/sitting-governance.ts:44 and lib/training-commercial-governance.ts:29: `if(!Number.isInteger(petCount)||petCount<1||petCount>Number(row.max_pets))`. lib/walking-governance.ts and lib/taxi-governance.ts use `!==1` and are already NaN-safe, which is the pattern to match.

findings.title: An anonymous caller can create a durable Boarding quote for a 100-year stay (Rs 10.2 crore) or a check-in in the year 2226
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p13.mjs posts to the real app/api/boarding-commercial/route.ts POST handler (no permission required per lib/api-gateway.ts:14) with packageCode 'boarding-24h', petCount 4, and scheduledEnd set 1, 10 and 100 years after scheduledStart; then a separate request with a check-in 200 years out. Rows read back from boarding_commercial_quotes. lib/boarding-governance.ts:47 checks only `endMs>startMs` and `startMs>Date.now()`; unitsFor at line 41 returns `Math.max(1,Math.ceil(hours/24))` with no ceiling.
findings.expected: NOBODY HAS DECIDED THIS. The open questions are: (1) what is the maximum bookable Boarding stay length - the code's only stated bounds are per-package max_hours for daycare and 'more than 10 hours' for overnight, with no upper limit; and (2) how far ahead may a check-in be scheduled - the only stated bound is 'must be in the future'. I am not picking numbers. Whatever the answers, createBoardingQuote should enforce them at line 47 the way it already enforces the lower bounds, so the rejection reads like the existing 409s rather than producing a nine-figure quote. The same two questions apply to Overnight Pet Sitting (lib/sitting-governance.ts `units`, identical `Math.ceil(hours/24)` with no cap).
findings.consequence: Every anonymous POST writes a durable boarding_commercial_quotes row, and the amount on it is unbounded: the reproduction stored a Rs 10,20,54,000 quote and a stay beginning in 2226. If such a quote is ever confirmed it produces a boarding_stays row and a provider_work_orders row spanning a century, which is what capacity, host-availability and revenue reads will then see. Even unconfirmed, the rows sit in the quote table and in any ops view or pipeline metric that sums or ranks open quotes, where a single nine-figure row will dominate. tests/commercial-quote-origin-surface.test.mjs justifies leaving these endpoints unauthenticated on the grounds that a quote is a harmless price-integrity record whose amount is 'computed server-side from the catalogue' - that argument holds for the unit price but not for the multiplier, which the caller controls without limit.
findings.rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger. The maximum Boarding/Sitting stay length and the maximum booking lead time are product decisions that do not exist anywhere in the code, the tests, or the seeded catalogue. Filed so the decision gets made rather than defaulted to infinity.
findings.suggested_fix: Once the two limits are decided, enforce them in createBoardingQuote (lib/boarding-governance.ts:47) and createSittingQuote (lib/sitting-governance.ts) next to the existing future-check, returning the same 409 shape as the other stay bounds, e.g. 'Boarding stays are limited to N nights' and 'Boarding cannot be booked more than N days ahead'. Do not merge a number until it is in the ledger.

findings.title: /api/live-price-quote returns price: null when quantity is a non-numeric JSON value
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p2.mjs calls the real POST handler of app/api/live-price-quote/route.ts (unauthenticated per lib/api-gateway.ts:15) with a valid packageCode/fallbackPrice/scheduledStart/cityId and quantity set to {}. The route validates packageCode, fallbackPrice, scheduledStart and cityId but passes `body.quantity` straight through. calculatePrice does `const quantity=Math.max(1,input.quantity??1)`: ?? does not catch a non-number, and Math.max(1,{}) is NaN, so base, running, beforeCoupon and finalPrice are all NaN and JSON.stringify emits null.
findings.expected: Either a 400 alongside the route's existing 'packageCode, fallbackPrice, scheduledStart and cityId are required' validation, or a quantity coerced with the same Number.isFinite discipline the route already applies to fallbackPrice. A 200 carrying price: null is the one answer a price endpoint must never give - the field is typed `price:number` in the resolver's return signature.
findings.consequence: The only customer-facing caller is app/mobile-app/grooming-flow.tsx:91, which does `if(active&&p.data)setLivePrice(p.data.price)` - a null response would blank or corrupt the displayed grooming price. That caller does not currently send quantity, so this is reachable today only by a direct call to the public endpoint, which is why it is P3 rather than higher. It is filed because the same `Math.max(1,input.quantity??1)` is the quantity path for app/api/pricing-quote (which does forward a client `quantity`) and because a typed number field silently becoming null is the shape of defect that surfaces later as an unexplained blank price.
findings.rule_source: lib/live-pricing-resolver.ts return type `Promise<{price:number;source:...}>` - the contract says price is a number. The route's own validation of fallbackPrice with Number.isFinite is the standard the quantity field is not held to.
findings.suggested_fix: In app/api/live-price-quote/route.ts, validate quantity the way fallbackPrice is validated (reject when present and not a finite positive integer), and harden calculatePrice itself: `const raw=Number(input.quantity); const quantity=Number.isFinite(raw)?Math.max(1,Math.floor(raw)):1;`. app/api/pricing-quote/route.ts forwards body.quantity with no check and needs the same.

findings.title: A Training programme costs the same for 1 pet as for 4 while the trainer's committed minutes quadruple
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/probe/p13.mjs posts to the real app/api/training-commercial/route.ts POST handler with packageCode 'training-16-pro' and petCount 1..4, a future scheduledStart and paymentMode 'prepaid', and prints totalAmount, minutesPerSession and sessions from the returned quote. totalAmount comes from `basePrice - coupon.discount` with no petCount factor; minutesPerSession is `petCount*(direct_minutes_per_pet + coaching_minutes_per_pet)`, i.e. 4 pets x (45+15) = 240 minutes per session. governTrainingBooking then requires exactly `sessions` reserved sessions, so the whole programme is committed at that per-session length.
findings.measured_before:
training-16-pro petCount=1: total=20000 minutesPerSession=60 sessions=16 totalTrainerMinutes=960
training-16-pro petCount=2: total=20000 minutesPerSession=120 sessions=16 totalTrainerMinutes=1920
training-16-pro petCount=3: total=20000 minutesPerSession=180 sessions=16 totalTrainerMinutes=2880
training-16-pro petCount=4: total=20000 minutesPerSession=240 sessions=16 totalTrainerMinutes=3840
findings.expected: NOBODY HAS DECIDED THIS. Every other vertical in the repo scales price with pet count in some explicit way - Boarding multiplies basePricePerPet by petCount, Sitting adds extra_pet_price per additional pet, Grooming has per-count bundle rows in lib/pricing-control-runtime.ts (groomingMultiPerPet) - while Training alone holds price flat and scales only duration. Both readings are defensible: a household programme priced per household, or a per-pet programme that should carry an extra-pet component. The schema hints at the latter: training_commercial_packages already carries per-pet minute columns (direct_minutes_per_pet, coaching_minutes_per_pet) but no extra-pet price column. I am not picking a number.
findings.consequence: At 4 pets the platform sells 3,840 trainer-minutes for the same Rs 20,000 it charges for 960 - a 4x swing in delivered cost with no revenue change, on a package the customer selects freely from the public /api/training-commercial endpoint. Whichever way the rule is meant to go, one side is currently wrong: either the trainer is being committed to four times the work unpaid, or a household is being told a 4-pet programme costs four times as much when it should not. It also lands in the provider's work order and any commission or payroll calculation keyed off session length. No customer-facing text in the quote explains that the price does not move with pet count.
findings.rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger. Question for the ledger: does a Training programme price per household or per pet, and if per pet, what is the extra-pet component? The per-pet minute columns exist in training_commercial_packages; a matching price column does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not change the arithmetic until the decision is recorded. If per-household is confirmed, state it in the quote response and the customer-facing copy so the flat price is deliberate and visible. If per-pet is confirmed, add an extra_pet_price column to training_commercial_packages alongside the existing per-pet minute columns and fold it into totalAmount in createTrainingQuote the way lib/sitting-governance.ts does with extra_pet_price.

findings.title: Grooming policy CREATE stores an unvalidated enforcement_mode; anything but exactly "enforce" silently becomes "observe", which forces 100% refund and waives every cancellation/reschedule rule
findings.pattern: H2 (unknown value normalised to the permissive branch) + gate polarity
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p10.mjs (probe) and /tmp/pj/p9.mjs (unit matrix).
1. installHooks(); fresh in-memory D1.
2. POST /api/grooming-commercial-policy with body {cityId:"city_blr",policyCode:"grooming-blr",enforcementMode:"Enforce",cancellationCutoffMinutes:1440,refundPercentBeforeCutoff:100,refundPercentAfterCutoff:0,rescheduleCutoffMinutes:1440,rescheduleAllowedAfterCutoff:false,maxReschedules:1,rescheduleFeeType:"flat",rescheduleFeeValue:500,multiPetMax:1,effectiveFrom:"2026-01-01",reason:"City launch policy"}
3. Read the stored row, then resolveGroomingPolicy(db,"city_blr","zone_1").
4. Seed a grooming booking BK_P1 (total 2000, status assigned, payment captured 2000) whose scheduled_start is now+60min - i.e. INSIDE the 1440-minute cutoff, so the policy prices the refund at 0%.
5. POST /api/grooming-booking-change {bookingId:"BK_P1",customerId:"cust_P",action:"cancel",reason:"late cancel"}.
6. PATCH the same policy with changes:{enforcement_mode:"Enforce"} for contrast.
findings.expected: Either (a) POST validates enforcement_mode against ['observe','enforce'] exactly as PATCH already does at app/api/grooming-commercial-policy/route.ts:11, returning 400 for "Enforce"; or (b) rowToPolicy/parsePolicySnapshot fail closed on an unrecognised value (treat unknown as 'enforce', or throw a configuration error) rather than defaulting to the permissive 'observe'. A refund of 0% was configured; a refund case of 0 (or a 409) is the expected outcome, not a 2000 refund case.
findings.consequence: Real money. A pricing manager launches a city with an enforcing cancellation policy - 24h cutoff, 0% late refund, one free reschedule, 500 reschedule fee, one pet max - and every one of those rules is silently inert because a single mis-cased string was accepted by the create endpoint that the update endpoint rejects. Every late customer cancellation raises a 100%-of-captured-amount refund case (2000 of 2000 measured), every reschedule is free and unlimited, and the multi-pet cap at app/api/canonical-bookings/route.ts:195 (guarded on enforcementMode==="enforce") never fires. Finance reconciles refunds it should never have owed; the operator reading the policy row sees "Enforce" while every API response says "observe", so the two surfaces disagree and nothing alerts.
findings.rule_source: The repository's own contract: PATCH on the same table already enforces ['observe','enforce'] (app/api/grooming-commercial-policy/route.ts:11), and lib/grooming-policy-governance.ts:42 evaluateBookingChange treats every non-"observe" value as enforcing. Only the CREATE path and the row parser disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same allow-list validation to POST (reject anything not in ['observe','enforce'], along with the numeric range checks PATCH performs), and change rowToPolicy/parsePolicySnapshot so an unrecognised enforcement_mode fails closed - either throw a configuration-required error like resolveGroomingPolicy already does for a missing policy, or map unknown to 'enforce'.

findings.title: decline / no_show / *_unavailable have no source-state guard in Sitting, Walking and Boarding: a completed or cancelled booking is regressed to reassignment_needed and can never be restored
findings.pattern: H11 (terminal state regressed by a late or out-of-order event)
findings.symbol: mutateSittingBooking / mutateWalkingBooking / mutateBoardingStay - the decline|*_unavailable|no_show branch
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p1.mjs, /tmp/pj/p2.mjs, /tmp/pj/p4.mjs, /tmp/pj/p5.mjs, /tmp/pj/p6.mjs, /tmp/pj/p13.mjs.
Sitting (lib): seed canonical_bookings BK_S1 service_code='pet_sitting' status='completed', work order 'completed', reservation 'completed'; call mutateSittingBooking(db,{bookingId:'BK_S1',action:'no_show',actorId:'prov_1',idempotencyKey:'k1',reason:'sitter never showed'}).
Sitting (HTTP): POST /api/sitting-lifecycle {bookingId:'BK_R1',action:'sitter_unavailable',idempotencyKey:'rk1',reason:'cannot make it'} against a booking already status='completed'. Repeat with status='cancelled'.
Walking: same shape with service_code='dog_walking' plus a walking_sessions row status='completed', action 'no_show'.
Boarding: seed boarding_stays ST1 status='completed' check_out_status='complete' on a booking status='completed'; mutateBoardingStay(action:'no_show').
Taxi control: identical setup with taxi_trips status='completed'.
Recovery attempt: after the sitting regression, try every lifecycle action to get back to 'completed' (/tmp/pj/p13.mjs).
findings.expected: The same guard Pet Taxi already applies (lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts:31): a recovery action must be refused with 409 when the booking/stay is already in a closed or in-flight state. A stay that has been delivered and checked out, or one that was cancelled and refunded, must not be movable into reassignment_needed by a provider-facing action; those cases belong to the incident workflow.
findings.consequence: A sitter, walker or boarding host - not staff - can regress a job they already delivered. `decline`, `sitter_unavailable`, `walker_unavailable` and `host_unavailable` are all in the provider action set of their routes (app/api/sitting-lifecycle/route.ts:8, app/api/walking-lifecycle/route.ts:7, app/api/boarding-stays/route.ts:9) and need only bookings.view plus ownership of their own assignment. The delivered booking lands in the Ops recovery queue with an open ops_escalation case, its scheduling reservation is cancelled, and no lifecycle action can return it to 'completed' - it is permanently stuck. Ops is asked to find a replacement provider for a stay that already ended; for Boarding the stay drops to recovery_pending and can be re-accepted, which re-locks host capacity for a window that is already in the past. Cancelled-and-refunded bookings are resurrected the same way. The guard that says 'Care plan cannot change after the Sitting booking is closed' is defeated as a side effect, because the booking is no longer 'completed'. Completed walking sessions stay 'completed' while their parent booking says reassignment_needed, so the walking read model and the canonical booking disagree.
findings.rule_source: lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts:31 states the rule explicitly for the identical action set: "Active/closed Pet Taxi trips require the safety incident workflow, not reassignment". Sitting/Walking/Boarding omit it. Whether 'cancelled' should also be terminal for these actions is a product decision -> decision ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: In each of the three modules, refuse the decline/unavailable/no_show branch when the current status is terminal or in-flight - mirror lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts:31, e.g. for Sitting reject when status is in ['in_progress','completed','cancelled'] and for Boarding when the stay is in ['in_progress','completed','cancelled'], routing those to the incident workflow instead.

findings.title: Lifecycle idempotency keys are not bound to the booking, stay, session or action: a colliding key silently drops the caller's mutation, returns HTTP 200, and hands back another entity's identifiers
findings.pattern: H4 (idempotency key not binding the full mutation context) + H14 (cross-entity identifiers returned to the wrong caller)
findings.symbol: priorResult / prior / duplicate - all lookup by idempotency_key alone
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p3.mjs (sitting lib), /tmp/pj/p6.mjs (sitting via HTTP), /tmp/pj/p11.mjs (walking, taxi, boarding), /tmp/pj/p12.mjs (training).
Sitting HTTP: seed BK_X (provider prov_X, customer cust_X) and BK_Y (provider prov_Y, customer cust_Y), both 'confirmed'.
  POST /api/sitting-lifecycle {bookingId:'BK_X',action:'accept',idempotencyKey:'COLLIDE'}
  POST /api/sitting-lifecycle {bookingId:'BK_Y',action:'check_out',idempotencyKey:'COLLIDE'}
Walking: WK_A accept key 'K'; then WK_B decline key 'K'.
Taxi: TX_A accept key 'KT'; then TX_B accept key 'KT'.
Boarding: stay SA decline key 'KB'; then stay SB check_out key 'KB'.
Training: session S3 accept key 'SHARED'; then session S4 cancel_session key 'SHARED'.
findings.expected: A replay must only be honoured when the stored key was recorded for the SAME entity and the SAME action - the tables already store booking_id/stay_id/action next to the key (e.g. sitting_action_keys(idempotency_key, booking_id, action)) but the lookup ignores both columns. A key recorded against a different booking/stay/session or a different action must be rejected (409 idempotency-key conflict), never replayed, and the stored result of an unrelated entity must never appear in the response body.
findings.consequence: Two independent failures at once. (1) Lost mutation reported as success: a sitter's check-out, a walker's decline, a host's check-out and a staff session cancellation each returned HTTP 200 and never happened - BK_Y stayed 'confirmed', SB stayed 'awaiting_host_acceptance', S4 stayed 'scheduled'. The caller and the audit trail both record a completed action; the operator will only discover it when the booking never settles. (2) Cross-tenant disclosure: the response handed customer/provider B another tenant's bookingId, providerId, stayId, tripId and recoveryId. The keys are free-form strings taken verbatim from the request body by every route (app/api/sitting-lifecycle/route.ts, walking-lifecycle, taxi-lifecycle, boarding-stays), so a caller can probe for them, and the namespace is global across all bookings and all customers.
findings.rule_source: Repository contract: the *_action_keys tables record booking_id/stay_id and action alongside the key, and lib/sitting-payment-governance.ts already implements the correct pattern - it binds a payment key to its quote and returns 403 PAYMENT_CAPTURE_REPLAY when a different key is presented (pinned by tests/sitting-payment-binding.test.mjs). The lifecycle modules do not follow it.
findings.suggested_fix: Change every prior/priorResult/duplicate lookup to select on (idempotency_key AND booking_id/stay_id/session_id AND action). When a row exists for the key but with a different entity or action, throw a 409 conflict rather than returning the stored result. For training, add session_id and event_type to the WHERE clause of the training_session_events lookup.

findings.title: A Grooming customer can self-cancel a booking that is in_service and receive a 100% refund case while the groomer is mid-appointment
findings.pattern: H11 / completion-gating: only 'completed' and 'cancelled' are change-locked, so every in-flight state is customer-cancellable
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p8.mjs.
1. Seed grooming policy for city_blr with the shipped default change_lock_statuses_json '["completed","cancelled"]' (this is the DDL default at lib/grooming-policy-governance.ts:22 and the value seedDefaultGroomingPolicy writes).
2. Seed canonical_bookings BK_G1 service_code='grooming' status='in_service' total_amount=2000, provider_work_orders status='assigned', booking_payments status='captured' amount=2000.
3. POST /api/grooming-booking-change {bookingId:'BK_G1',customerId:'cust_G',action:'cancel',reason:'changed my mind'} as the owning customer.
4. Re-read canonical_bookings, provider_work_orders, booking_payments, booking_refund_cases.
findings.expected: Undecided in this repository - the correct behaviour is a product decision nobody has recorded for Grooming. The open question is: once a Grooming booking has left 'assigned' (on_the_way / arrived / in_service), is customer self-cancellation still a self-serve action at full refund, or must it route to an Operations incident workflow the way Pet Sitting does? Whatever is decided, in_service must not be treated the same as a booking that has not started.
findings.consequence: The groomer is physically at the customer's home with the service underway; the customer taps cancel and the platform (a) flips the provider's work order to 'cancelled' out from under them mid-job, (b) cancels the scheduling reservation, and (c) raises a refund case for the entire captured amount (2000 of 2000 measured) with zero cancellation fee. The provider has delivered part of a service that the system now records as never having happened, and Finance is handed a full refund to process. `on_the_way` and `arrived` behave identically.
findings.rule_source: NONE -> decision ledger for Grooming. The adjacent module states the opposite rule for the same situation: lib/sitting-finance-governance.ts refuses with "In-progress Sitting cancellation requires an Operations incident workflow" (pinned by tests/sitting-gate3.test.mjs). Grooming's shipped default lock list is only ["completed","cancelled"], so the two services disagree about the same customer action.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pick a refund number here - record the decision first. Mechanically, the change is to the change-lock list / evaluateBookingChange: either add the in-flight statuses ('on_the_way','arrived','in_service') to the Grooming change lock so the route returns 409 and the customer is routed to the incident/refund workflow, or introduce an explicit in-progress branch with its own recorded refund policy. Until the decision exists, flagging in_service cancellations for Operations review rather than auto-raising a 100% refund case would at least stop the money moving on an unrecorded rule.

findings.title: Sitting `accept` work-order-match guard is a tautology when the work order is missing or has an empty provider_id, so the booking is marked assigned with no accepted work order
findings.pattern: Absent treated as satisfied (the `|| providerId` fallback compares the value against itself)
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p7.mjs.
A) Seed BK_N1 service_code='pet_sitting' status='confirmed' provider_id='prov_1', then DELETE the provider_work_orders row. Call mutateSittingBooking(action:'accept').
B) Same setup for dog_walking (BK_N2) as the control.
C) BK_N3: leave the work order but set its provider_id='prov_OTHER' (guard should fire).

findings.expected: The identical guard in lib/walking-lifecycle.ts:31 - `if(String(booking.provider_id)!==String(booking.work_order_provider_id))` - fails closed on the same inputs and returns 409. Sitting should behave the same: a NULL (LEFT JOIN miss) or empty work-order provider is exactly the drift the guard exists to catch, so it must refuse, not pass.
findings.consequence: The guard is there to stop a sitter accepting a booking whose canonical work order has drifted away from them, and it does not fire in the one case that most needs it. The booking is written to 'assigned' and the sitter is told the acceptance succeeded, while `UPDATE provider_work_orders SET status='accepted'` changes zero rows. Every Sitting surface that joins provider_work_orders (listSittingBookings, the Ops queue, provider settlement) then shows a null work-order status against a booking that claims to be assigned - two surfaces disagreeing, with no error anywhere. A work order carrying an empty provider_id is likewise accepted and stamped 'accepted' for a provider it does not name.
findings.rule_source: Repository contract: lib/walking-lifecycle.ts:31 implements the same invariant for the same action and fails closed. The `||providerId` fallback in Sitting defeats it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the fallback and compare the raw values, refusing when the work order is absent: `if(!booking.work_order_id || String(booking.work_order_provider_id||"")!==providerId) throw new Response(...,{status:409})` - matching lib/walking-lifecycle.ts:31.

findings.title: Training provider no-show grace-period gate passes when scheduled_start is unparseable, because the NaN comparison is false
findings.pattern: H2 (NaN comparison silently satisfies a gate)
findings.reproduction:
/tmp/pj/p12.mjs.
1. Seed training_programmes PG1 (total_sessions 4) and two training_sessions, each scheduled 30 days in the future with a matching scheduling_reservations row.
2. S1 keeps its valid future scheduled_start; call mutateTrainingSession(action:'no_show', reason:'customer absent') with no staffOverride - the grace gate should refuse.
3. S2 is identical except `UPDATE training_sessions SET scheduled_start='' WHERE id='S2'`; call the same mutation.
4. Re-read training_sessions, training_programmes and scheduling_reservations.
findings.expected: An unparseable or missing scheduled_start makes the grace period unknowable, so the gate must refuse (fail closed) - the same 409 S1 receives - rather than let the comparison evaluate to false and record the no-show. `Number.isFinite(startMs)` must be checked before the comparison, as lib/stay-split-payments.ts:24 already does for the same kind of parse.
findings.consequence: A session that has not started - and whose start time the system cannot even read - is recorded as a customer no-show. The session status becomes 'no_show', the scheduling reservation becomes 'no_show', the programme is advanced to 'in_progress' with no_show_sessions incremented, and a TSR recovery case is opened carrying consumption:'pending_policy' - i.e. the customer is put in line to have a paid session burned for a class that never happened. findings.title: Second expiry of a reservation lease releases capacity but leaves the assignment decision 'assigned' and the provider offer 'pending'
findings.reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/sched/p10.mjs.
1. Customer reserves group G1 with a real session (preferredProviderId groom_kiran, a commission provider, so an offer row is created).
2. cleanupExpiredReservationLeases(db, now+16min) — the normal 15-minute lease expiry.
3. Ops POST /api/uat-scheduling {action:'reassign', groupId:'G1', reason:'customer called back, re-offer the slot'} — succeeds, new reservation, new 15-minute lease, new pending offer.
4. cleanupExpiredReservationLeases(db, now+40min) — the second expiry.
findings.expected: A release either happens completely or not at all. If the reservations are cancelled, the decision must move to 'expired' and the pending offer must be cancelled — exactly as cleanup#1 did. The function must also not report {groups:1,reservations:1} for a partial release.
findings.consequence: After the second expiry the capacity ledger says nothing is reserved (both reservations cancelled) while the Ops scheduling decision surface still says the group is assigned to groom_arun, attributed to the operator who reassigned it, and groom_arun's partner app still shows a live pending job offer for a slot that no longer exists. Ops believes the customer has a groomer; groom_arun believes they have an offer to accept; the slot is simultaneously free for anyone else to take. The idempotency row scheduling_reservation_lease_cleanup(group_id PRIMARY KEY) is keyed by group alone and holds the FIRST release's released_at, so statements 3 and 4 — both predicated on `EXISTS (... c.released_at=?)` bound to the current now — silently match nothing on every subsequent release of that group. The function still returns groups:1 because its counter reads statement[1] (the reservations UPDATE), which is not gated on the cleanup row.
findings.rule_source: The module's own contract, asserted in tests/scheduling-reservation-leases.test.mjs: after a release the decision is 'expired'/'system:reservation-lease-cleanup' and the offer is 'cancelled'. That test only ever releases a group once.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the idempotency row by (group_id, released_at) or by a release attempt id rather than group_id alone, or gate statements 3 and 4 on the same predicate as statement 2 instead of on an exact released_at match. Return counts derived from the gated statements.

findings.title: A provider is told 'available, 0 restrictions remaining' while a staff-imposed suspension for a future date is still active
findings.reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/sched/p18.mjs.
1. Ops POST /api/provider-capacity-control {action:'block_time', providerId:'groom_arun', startsAt:'2026-11-26T00:00:00.000Z', endsAt:'2026-11-26T23:00:00.000Z', reason:'ops imposed suspension pending KYC'} -> 201, active provider_unavailability row created_by closure-admin@pawspace.test.
2. groom_arun, with their own provider session cookie, POST /api/provider-availability {providerId:'groom_arun', available:true, reason:'I am available again'}.
3. Staff (no provider cookie, staff header identity) POST the same body.
4. A customer then tries to book groom_arun for 2026-11-26T04:00Z.
findings.expected: The documented contract of this function is that a restriction imposed by somebody else 'stays standing... and the caller needs to know it did not take effect'. A future-dated active suspension must be counted in restrictionsRemaining and must make `available` false. Staff clearing through this route must either actually clear the future window or report that it did not.
findings.consequence: Both the clearing UPDATE and the restrictionsRemaining COUNT are bound to `nowIso` with `starts_at<=? AND ends_at>?`, so every restriction that has not started yet is invisible to them — an absent-at-this-instant restriction is treated as no restriction. A provider suspended for next week opens their partner app, toggles Available, and is told they are available with zero restrictions; they plan their week on a figure that is false. A staff member trying to lift the suspension through this route gets 200 available:true with windowsCleared:0 and believes it took effect; the row is still active and the provider remains unbookable (only the capacity-control unblock_time action actually clears it, and only that action also cancels the BLOCK-* capacity reservation the block created). findings.suggested_fix: Count and clear on window overlap with the period being asserted, not on the current instant: `ends_at>?` with now, dropping `starts_at<=?`, or take an explicit as-of range. Report `available:false` whenever any active window remains, and surface windowsCleared:0 as an explicit 'no effect' outcome rather than a 200 success.

DB row2: {"id":"groom_kiran","capacity":"abc","max_daily_jobs":"lots"}
getGovernedProvider2: {"id":"groom_kiran",...,"capacity":null,"travelBufferMinutes":30,"maxDailyJobs":null}   (null is JSON's rendering of NaN)

findings.title: uat-scheduling's cancel/reassign/assign/manual actions authenticate but never authorize, and never check group ownership
findings.reproduction:
node --experimental-strip-types /tmp/sched/p5.mjs and /tmp/sched/p6.mjs.
p5: CUST-VICTIM reserves group GRP-VICTIM. Then CUST-ATTACKER — a plain customer platform session, permissions ['pricing.view','scheduling.book'] — POSTs {action:'cancel', groupId:'GRP-VICTIM', customerId:'CUST-ATTACKER', reason:'not mine'} and then {action:'reassign', groupId:'GRP-VICTIM', ...} directly to the route handler.
p6: the same requests run through lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest.
findings.expected: The route calls `resolveActor(request)` — it establishes WHO the caller is and then never asks WHETHER they may act. It should call `requirePermission(actor,'scheduling.manage')` before operateAssignment, matching the permission lib/api-gateway.ts already declares for this path, and operateAssignment should verify the target group's customer_id/city before mutating it.
findings.consequence: Reproduced at the route: a customer session cancels and then reassigns a different customer's confirmed scheduling group, and the audit row records the attacker as the actor on the victim's decision. In the deployed worker this specific path is stopped by lib/api-gateway.ts (verified: 403 Permission denied for both a customer and a provider session), so the gateway is the ONLY control. That makes the gateway a single point of failure for a cross-tenant write — precisely the condition app/api/scheduling-rules/route.ts documents as a defect and fixed for its sibling ('one edit to the allowlist or the map and the handler would happily serve and mutate for anybody'). uat-scheduling is the higher-value target of the two and carries no such check. Reachable today by anything that reaches the handler without the gateway: a direct Next handler invocation, a future route added to the gateway's non-/api space, or any change to the body-shape-dependent mapping at lib/api-gateway.ts:124 (the mapping is decided by parsing the request body, so a body the gateway parses differently than the route downgrades the permission to scheduling.book).
