findings.suggested_fix: Add `requirePermission(actor,'scheduling.manage')` immediately after resolveActor for any non-reserve action, and have operateAssignment load the group's reservations and refuse when the group is outside the actor's city/tenant scope.

findings.title: The gate covering the capacity-safe replacement engine asserts source text only and passes while the engine returns the failing provider
findings.symbol: gate 5 recovery precedes capacity safe replacement
findings.reproduction: node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/universal-gps-lateness-recovery.test.mjs passes. The suite's only handle on lib/universal-replacement-recovery.ts is `const replacement=read('lib/universal-replacement-recovery.ts')` followed by `for (const m of ['loadGovernedProviders','scheduling_availability','scheduling_reservations','travelBufferMinutes','maxDailyJobs','requiresAcceptance']) assert.match(replacement,new RegExp(m))`. selectCapacitySafeReplacement is never imported or called anywhere in the repository's tests.
findings.measured_before: tests/universal-gps-lateness-recovery.test.mjs:1-5 reads six files as strings; gate 5 asserts six identifiers appear in the text of lib/universal-replacement-recovery.ts and that /no_capacity_safe_candidate/ appears in the route text. It passes on the frozen base at the same time as /tmp/sched/p11.mjs measures 'C. route select_replacement with NO providerId -> 200 {"provider":"groom_arun","status":"replacement_eligible","checks":{...all true}}' — groom_arun being the provider the replacement was for.
findings.expected: A gate named 'capacity safe replacement' must execute selectCapacitySafeReplacement against a real D1-backed booking and assert the returned candidate: that the excluded provider is absent, that a provider at their daily cap is skipped, that a provider with a conflicting reservation inside the travel buffer is skipped, and that a missing exclusion is refused rather than ignored.
findings.consequence: The named safety gate for this domain's recovery engine gives no evidence about behaviour. Every defect reported above in selectCapacitySafeReplacement is live underneath a passing gate, so the readiness signal it produces is unearned. The presence of the string 'maxDailyJobs' is what is currently being certified.
findings.rule_source: The repository's own convention: tests/scheduling-reservation-leases.test.mjs and tests/lane2-core-integration-boundaries.test.mjs execute their modules against a real node:sqlite D1 shim; the same technique applies here unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite gate 5 to import selectCapacitySafeReplacement through installWorkersHooks and assert on returned candidates against seeded canonical_bookings / scheduling_availability / scheduling_reservations rows, keeping the text assertions only for the documentation files.

domains.coverage_gaps:
WHAT I COULD NOT EXECUTE OR DID NOT REACH:

1. Real Cloudflare D1 semantics. Every probe ran against the repository's own node:sqlite DatabaseSync shim (tests/helpers/grooming-journey-harness.mjs), which serialises db.batch() inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The two race findings were produced by driving that shim's own `beforeBatch` interleave hook, which models "request B completed its read-decide-write between A's decision and A's commit". That is the correct model for two concurrent Worker isolates against one D1 database, but I did not execute it against real D1, so the timing window's width in production is unmeasured. The defect itself — the committing INSERT guard is strictly narrower than the eligibility rules — is a static property of the SQL and does not depend on the engine.

2. The deployed edge path. I executed lib/api-gateway.ts authorizeApiRequest and lib/session-api-gateway.ts mappings directly, but worker/index.ts's fetch handler was not run end to end (it needs the vinext app-router entry and a Workers runtime). The authorization finding is therefore reported with its real reachability stated: blocked by the gateway today, absent at the route.

3. External providers are all absent, as expected. Payment capture in /tmp/sched/p8.mjs went through app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox, which is the repository's own sandbox transport — it proves OUR booking/payment state machine accepted a past-dated service, not that a real gateway captured money.

4. Not probed to a conclusion: (a) the IST-vs-UTC day boundary divergence between backend/src/scheduling.ts dateKey() (IST, +330m) and lib/universal-replacement-recovery.ts's `substr(scheduled_start,1,10)` (UTC) — I confirmed the two definitions differ by reading and executing both, but did not construct a booking that crosses IST midnight to show a concrete wrong daily count, so I am not filing it; (b) recurring dog_training/dog_walking groups (occurrences/cadenceDays/weekdays) beyond validating that 0, negative and string inputs are rejected or degrade safely — I did not test lease expiry or reassignment against a multi-occurrence group; (c) duplicate petIds inflating capacity_units on boarding (over-consumes capacity, so it fails safe); (d) lib/background-scheduler.ts sweeps other than confirming, by reading worker/index.ts's scheduled handler, that cleanupExpiredReservationLeases IS wired to the 5-minute cron (so there is no H15 "never fires" defect there); (e) provider_assignment_offers expiry — no sweep expires a pending offer on the cron, only app/api/provider-assignment-recovery's explicit `timeout` action does, which I did not drive.

5. Base SHA note: HEAD is b113f81, one commit ahead of the stated frozen base 53101a1f. `git diff 53101a1f..HEAD` touches only ptja/PTJA-BASELINE.json and tests/ptja-identity-spine.test.mjs — every file in this domain is identical at both revisions, so all findings apply to the frozen base.
